Downstream analysis for the networks created using FastSpar.

These scripts were written by Chen Xi Ye Xu as part of her Master´s Thesis 
for UAM - Master of Bioinformatics and Computational Biology. 

GEPHI INFO
After running this code we can use the results inside Gephi to visualize the network better!

In linux you download from Gephi (https://gephi.org/) the folder, unzip it, go to bin and then use ./gephi. If it doesn´t work, it is probably because you need to run chmod 777 gephi first. 

Gephi accepts .tsv files!


# Loading necessary libraries. 
```{r}
#We can clean up the variables. 
rm(list = ls())

#For reproducibility
set.seed(123)

#Packages available through CRAN
cran_packages <- c(
  "tidyverse",
  "data.table",
  "vegan",
  "ggpubr",
  "CooccurrenceAffinity",
  "igraph",
  "ggraph",
  "tidygraph")

#Packages available through Bioconductor
bioc_packages <- c(
  "microbiome",
  "phyloseq")


##############################################################
##Check and install CRAN packages
##############################################################
missing_cran <- cran_packages[
  !cran_packages %in% rownames(installed.packages())]

if (length(missing_cran) > 0) {
  cat(
    "Installing missing CRAN packages:\n",
    paste(missing_cran, collapse = ", "),
    "\n\n")
  install.packages(
    missing_cran,

} else {
  cat("All required CRAN packages are already installed.\n\n")}


##############################################################
##Check and install Bioconductor packages
##############################################################
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
  cat("BiocManager is not installed. Installing it now...\n\n")
  install.packages("BiocManager")}

missing_bioc <- bioc_packages[
  !bioc_packages %in% rownames(installed.packages())]

if (length(missing_bioc) > 0) {
  cat(
    "Installing missing Bioconductor packages:\n",
    paste(missing_bioc, collapse = ", "),
    "\n\n")
  BiocManager::install(
    missing_bioc,
    ask = FALSE,
    update = FALSE)
} else {
  cat("All required Bioconductor packages are already installed.\n\n")}


##############################################################
##Load all packages
##############################################################
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidyverse)
  library(data.table)
  library(vegan)

cat("All required packages were installed/loaded successfully!\n")
```

```{r}
metadata <- read.table(

  header = TRUE,

#Paths to the FastSpar output files generated by the bash script.
FILTERED_TSV <- file.path(NETWORK_DIR, "Matrices", "abundance_matrix_genus_filtered.tsv")
CORR_FILE    <- file.path(NETWORK_DIR, "correlation.tsv")
PVAL_FILE    <- file.path(NETWORK_DIR, "pvalues.tsv")
```

## 3) Loading FastSpar data.
```{r}
#Reading FastSpar correlation and p-value matrices.
cor_mat <- as.matrix(
  read.table(
    CORR_FILE,
    header = TRUE,
    row.names = 1,
    sep = "\t",
    check.names = FALSE,
    comment.char = ""))

p_mat <- as.matrix(
  read.table(
    PVAL_FILE,
    header = TRUE,
    row.names = 1,
    sep = "\t",
    check.names = FALSE,
    comment.char = ""))

#Validating that dimensions and names match perfectly
stopifnot(identical(rownames(cor_mat), rownames(p_mat)))
stopifnot(identical(colnames(cor_mat), colnames(p_mat)))
stopifnot(identical(rownames(cor_mat), colnames(cor_mat)))

#Function to clean taxonomy names with a hierarchical fallback.
clean_tax_name <- function(x) {
  #Split the full taxonomy string by semicolons
  levels <- unlist(strsplit(x, ";\\s*"))
  
  #Names considered uninformative or unclassified.
  uninf_terms <- c("", "uncultured", "unclassified", "unknown", 
                   "incertae_sedis", "ambiguous", "metagenome", 
                   "_", "__", "___")
  
  #Walk backwards from genus to domain if the name is empty.
  chosen_name <- "Unclassified"
  for (lvl in rev(levels)) {
    #Remove rank prefixes like g__, f__, o__, etc.
    clean_val <- sub("^[a-zA-Z]+__?", "", lvl)
    clean_val <- trimws(clean_val)
    
    #Check if the level contains valid information.
    if (!(tolower(clean_val) %in% uninf_terms) && clean_val != "") {
      chosen_name <- clean_val
      break
    }}
  return(chosen_name)}

#Apply hierarchical cleaning and ensure uniqueness across all row/column names
cleaned_rownames <- sapply(rownames(cor_mat), clean_tax_name)

#Some taxa can coincide if they had to go backwards so we add a number 
# after it to distinguish them. 
unique_rownames <- make.unique(cleaned_rownames, sep = "_")
rownames(cor_mat) <- unique_rownames
colnames(cor_mat) <- unique_rownames
rownames(p_mat) <- unique_rownames
colnames(p_mat) <- unique_rownames

#Converting matrices to long format edge lists.
cor_df <- cor_mat %>%
  as.data.frame(check.names = FALSE) %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("Taxon1") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-Taxon1, names_to = "Taxon2", values_to = "r")

p_df <- p_mat %>%
  as.data.frame(check.names = FALSE) %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("Taxon1") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-Taxon1, names_to = "Taxon2", values_to = "p")

#Joining correlation and p-values and applying significance and strength filters.
r_cutoff <- 0.2
p_cutoff <- 0.05

edges_all_raw <- cor_df %>%
  dplyr::left_join(p_df, by = c("Taxon1", "Taxon2")) %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    Taxon1 < Taxon2,
    !is.na(r),
    !is.na(p),
    abs(r) >= r_cutoff,
    p <= p_cutoff
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(sign = ifelse(r > 0, "positive", "negative"))


cat("FINISHED 3) Loading FastSpar data.")
```


## 4) Filtering weaker connections.
```{r}
#Filtering parameters for a more focused, robust network.
r_cutoff <- 0.4  

#Threshold must use adjusted p-value. 
p_adj_cutoff <- 0.05

#Apply correction to p-values!
# Benjamini-Hochberg = BH/fdr
# Holm = holm
p_df <- p_df %>%
  dplyr::mutate(p_adj = p.adjust(p, method = "BH"))

#Joining correlation and adjusted p-values with stricter filters.
edges_all_raw <- cor_df %>%
  dplyr::left_join(p_df, by = c("Taxon1", "Taxon2")) %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    Taxon1 < Taxon2,
    !is.na(r),
    !is.na(p_adj),
    abs(r) >= r_cutoff,
    p_adj <= p_adj_cutoff
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(sign = ifelse(r > 0, "positive", "negative"))


cat("FINISHED 4) Filtering weaker connections.")
```





## 5) Creating node and edge tables for Gephi export and network construction.
```{r}
#Formatting edges table for Gephi and downstream analyses
edges_all <- data.frame(
  Source = edges_all_raw$Taxon1,
  Target = edges_all_raw$Taxon2,
  Type = "Undirected",
  Weight = round(abs(edges_all_raw$r), 6),
  r = round(edges_all_raw$r, 6),
  p = signif(edges_all_raw$p, 6),
  sign = edges_all_raw$sign,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

#Splitting into positive and negative edge subsets!
#Positive means they usually appear together and negative
# that they usually don´t.
edges_pos <- dplyr::filter(edges_all, sign == "positive")
edges_neg <- dplyr::filter(edges_all, sign == "negative")

#Function to calculate node degrees and strengths dynamically
make_nodes <- function(edges_df) {
  if (nrow(edges_df) == 0) {
    return(data.frame(
      Id = character(),
      Label = character(),
      Degree = integer(),
      Strength = numeric(),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    ))}
  
  nds <- unique(c(edges_df$Source, edges_df$Target))
  deg <- table(c(edges_df$Source, edges_df$Target))
  str <- tapply(rep(edges_df$Weight, 2),
                c(edges_df$Source, edges_df$Target), sum)
  
  out <- data.frame(
    Id = nds,
    Label = nds,
    Degree = as.integer(deg[nds]),
    Strength = round(as.numeric(str[nds]), 6),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  
  out$Degree[is.na(out$Degree)] <- 0L
  out$Strength[is.na(out$Strength)] <- 0
  out}

#Generating node tables for all, positive, and negative networks
nodes_all <- make_nodes(edges_all)
nodes_pos <- make_nodes(edges_pos)
nodes_neg <- make_nodes(edges_neg)

message("Total edges: ", nrow(edges_all), " | Positive: ", 
        nrow(edges_pos), " | Negative: ", nrow(edges_neg))


cat(" FINISHED 5) Creating node and edge tables for Gephi export and network construction.")
```


## 6) Exporting edge and node tables for all, positive and negative networks.
```{r}
#Exporting edge and node tables for Gephi.
#Creating subdirectories inside the Gephi folder.
dir.create(file.path(GEPHI_DIR, "All"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(file.path(GEPHI_DIR, "Positive"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(file.path(GEPHI_DIR, "Negative"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

#Writing edge tables to Gephi folder.
write.table(
  edges_all,
  file.path(GEPHI_DIR, "All", "fastspar_genus_edges_all.tsv"),
  sep = "\t",

  row.names = FALSE)

write.table(

  file.path(GEPHI_DIR, "Positive", "fastspar_genus_edges_positive.tsv"),
  sep = "\t",

write.table(
  edges_neg,
  file.path(GEPHI_DIR, "Negative", "fastspar_genus_edges_negative.tsv"),

  quote = FALSE,

#Writing node tables to Gephi folder.

  nodes_all,
  file.path(GEPHI_DIR, "All", "fastspar_genus_nodes_all.tsv"),
  sep = "\t",

write.table(

write.table(
  nodes_neg,
  file.path(GEPHI_DIR, "Negative", "fastspar_genus_nodes_negative.tsv"),
  sep = "\t",
  quote = FALSE,
  row.names = FALSE)

message("Gephi tables successfully exported to: ", GEPHI_DIR)


cat("FINISHED 6) Exporting edge and node tables for all, positive and negative networks.")
```


## 7) Plotting correlation networks.
```{r}
#Function to plot correlation networks using ggraph.
plot_correlation_network <- function(edges_out, title, outfile_prefix) {
  for (sign_label in c("positive", "negative")) {
    edges_sub <- subset(edges_out, sign == sign_label)
    
    if (nrow(edges_sub) == 0) {
      message("Sin aristas ", sign_label, " para graficar: ", outfile_prefix)
      next}
    
    nodes_sub <- tibble::tibble(
      name = unique(c(edges_sub$Source, edges_sub$Target)),
      label = unique(c(edges_sub$Source, edges_sub$Target)))
    
    g <- igraph::graph_from_data_frame(
      d = edges_sub[, c("Source", "Target", "r", "Weight")],
      vertices = nodes_sub,
      directed = FALSE)
    
    V(g)$degree <- igraph::degree(g)
    g_tbl <- tidygraph::as_tbl_graph(g)
    
    edge_color <- if (sign_label == "positive") "firebrick3" else "steelblue3"
    
    p <- ggraph::ggraph(g_tbl, layout = "fr") +
      ggraph::geom_edge_link(aes(width = Weight), color = edge_color, alpha = 0.4) +
      ggraph::scale_edge_width(range = c(0.2, 2), guide = "none") +
      ggraph::geom_node_point(aes(size = degree), color = "grey20", alpha = 0.9) +
      ggplot2::scale_size_continuous(range = c(2, 8), guide = "none") +
      ggraph::geom_node_text(aes(label = label), size = 2.5, repel = TRUE, max.overlaps = Inf) +
      ggraph::theme_graph() +
      ggplot2::labs(title = title, subtitle = paste(sign_label, "correlations"))
    
    outfile <- paste0(outfile_prefix, "_", sign_label, ".png")
    ggplot2::ggsave(outfile, plot = p, width = 10, height = 10, dpi = 300)
    message("Figura guardada: ", outfile)}}

#Executing network plotting.
plot_correlation_network(
  edges_out = edges_all,
  title = "FastSpar Genus Correlation Network",
  outfile_prefix = file.path(FIGURES_OUT_DIR, "fastspar_genus"))


cat("FINISHED 7) Plotting correlation networks.")
```


## 8) Plot the network interactively in R!
```{r}
#Plotting the network interactively or inline in RStudio.
#Change here for positive/negative network: "positive" or "negative".
sign_type <- "positive"

edges_sub <- subset(edges_all, sign == sign_type)

#Function to strip all higher taxonomy levels and prefixes (e.g., g__).
clean_tax_name <- function(x) {
  x <- sub(".*;\\s*", "", x)
  x <- sub("^[a-zA-Z]+__?", "", x)
  return(x)}

#Clean Source and Target columns
edges_sub$Source <- clean_tax_name(edges_sub$Source)
edges_sub$Target <- clean_tax_name(edges_sub$Target)

nodes_sub <- tibble::tibble(
  name = unique(c(edges_sub$Source, edges_sub$Target)),
  label = unique(c(edges_sub$Source, edges_sub$Target)))

g <- igraph::graph_from_data_frame(
  d = edges_sub[, c("Source", "Target", "r", "Weight")],
  vertices = nodes_sub,
  directed = FALSE)

V(g)$degree <- igraph::degree(g)
g_tbl <- tidygraph::as_tbl_graph(g)

#Dynamic styling and labels based on sign_type.
edge_color <- if (sign_type == "positive") "firebrick3" else "steelblue3"
net_title  <- paste0("FastSpar ", tools::toTitleCase(sign_type), " Correlation Network")
net_sub    <- paste(sign_type, "correlations at genus level")

#Render the plot directly in the R studio plot window.
ggraph::ggraph(g_tbl, layout = "fr") +
  ggraph::geom_edge_link(aes(width = Weight), color = edge_color, alpha = 0.4) +
  ggraph::scale_edge_width(range = c(0.2, 2), guide = "none") +
  ggraph::geom_node_point(aes(size = degree), color = "grey20", alpha = 0.9) +
  ggplot2::scale_size_continuous(range = c(2, 8), guide = "none") +
  ggraph::geom_node_text(aes(label = label), size = 2.5, repel = TRUE, max.overlaps = Inf) +
  ggraph::theme_graph() +
  ggplot2::labs(title = net_title, subtitle = net_sub)


cat("FINISHED 8) Plot the network interactively in R!")
```
